title: Word problem for one-relation monoids
credit: S. I. Adian (posed c. 1960); reduction by Adian and G. U. Oganesyan
premise_risks: the precise form of the Adian-Oganesyan reduction (bUa=a) was taken from secondary knowledge of the survey, not verified from the full text in this check
famous within combinatorial semigroup theory; vetter should judge 'famous problem in disguise' (it is stated directly, not disguised)
plain: Take a monoid with a single defining relation u = v between two words. Is its word problem always decidable: for each such monoid, is there an algorithm that, given two words, decides whether they are equal in it? This is open even though the corresponding question for one-relator groups was settled long ago.
math: For a finite alphabet $A$ and $u,v\in A^*$, let $\equiv_{u,v}$ be the smallest congruence on $A^*$ containing $(u,v)$. Problem: does every one-relation monoid $\mathrm{Mon}\langle A\mid u=v\rangle$ have decidable word problem, i.e. is $\{(w_1,w_2): w_1\equiv_{u,v}w_2\}$ decidable for every fixed $A,u,v$? Board Claim: yes. (Uniform variant: the set of all $(A,u,v,w_1,w_2)$ with $w_1\equiv_{u,v}w_2$ is decidable. By Adian--Oganesyan (1978; two-generator form 1987) it suffices to treat $\mathrm{Mon}\langle a,b\mid bUa=aVa\rangle$ and $\mathrm{Mon}\langle a,b\mid bUa=a\rangle$, $U,V\in\{a,b\}^*$; both cases remain open. Undecidability for one fixed such monoid settles the problem negatively.)
review_note: Known: Decidable for special monoids <A|r=1> (Adian 1960; Makanin's reduction to the group of units), for Adian's left- or right-cycle-free presentations (u and v differ in first letter, or in last letter), and many subcases (Adian-Oganesyan 1987, Lallement 1974, Kobayashi, and Nyberg-Brodda's monadic results). Adian-Oganesyan reduced the general problem to <a,b | bUa = a>. Surveys: Nyberg-Brodda, 'The word problem for one-relation monoids: a survey', Semigroup Forum 103 (2021), arXiv:2105.02853. Related undecidability: one-relator inverse monoids (R. D. Gray, Invent. Math. 2020). Status reconfirmed open in Gray-Steinberg arXiv:2507.04819 (v2 March 2026) and Foniqi-Gray-Nyberg-Brodda (Canad. J. Math. 2024, arXiv:2305.15672), where the related prefix-membership problem is shown undecidable for some positive one-relator groups.
